title: How acids react with metals and carbonates
examples: What do you get when an acid reacts with a metal?
How do you test for carbon dioxide?
What salt does sulfuric acid make?

explain.say: Drop a strip of magnesium into acid, and it fizzes. Drop a piece of chalk in, and it fizzes too! Are they making the same gas? Look at the board. You can see the two reactions side by side.

draw.name: x-compare

explain.say: See the left side? When an acid meets a reactive metal, like magnesium or zinc, it makes a salt and hydrogen gas. Magnesium plus hydrochloric acid gives magnesium chloride plus hydrogen. How could you prove the gas is hydrogen?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Both fizz, but the gases differ

explain.say: Hold a lit splint near it: hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop! Now look at the right side. Carbonates, like chalk, marble and baking soda, make a salt, water and carbon dioxide. What test do you think spots carbon dioxide?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Both fizz, but the gases differ

explain.say: Bubble it through limewater, which turns milky! Now look at the naming groups. The acid gives the salt its second name: sulfuric acid makes sulfates, so zinc plus sulfuric acid gives zinc sulfate. What would you get from magnesium and hydrochloric acid?

draw.question: Name the salt from the acid

explain.say: Magnesium chloride! Brilliant. Wow: marble is calcium carbonate, so marble statues and buildings can be slowly eaten by acid rain in exactly this way, fizzing out carbon dioxide. Look closely at old marble near you, and you may see the damage.

faq.q: What do you get when an acid reacts with a metal?
faq.a: Acid plus metal gives a salt plus hydrogen. For example, zinc plus sulfuric acid gives zinc sulfate plus hydrogen.

faq.q: What do you get when an acid reacts with a carbonate?
faq.a: Acid plus carbonate gives a salt, water and carbon dioxide. Calcium carbonate plus hydrochloric acid gives calcium chloride, water and carbon dioxide.

faq.q: How do you test for hydrogen?
faq.a: Hold a lit splint at the mouth of the test tube. Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop.
asks: What is the squeaky pop test?

faq.q: How do you test for carbon dioxide?
faq.a: Bubble the gas through limewater, which is calcium hydroxide solution. It turns milky if carbon dioxide is present.

faq.q: Does copper react with dilute acid?
faq.a: No. Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not react with dilute hydrochloric or sulfuric acid. Silver and gold do not either.
asks: Which metals do not react with acid?

facts: Metal + acid → salt + hydrogen; carbonate + acid → salt + water + carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky because it forms insoluble calcium carbonate.
